title: Documenting the booking system
idea: Design documentation records what the system does, which classes do it and why, using a short README, UML diagrams and doc comments on public methods.
points: A class diagram shows classes, their key members and how they relate.
A sequence diagram shows one use case, such as booking a room, in order.
Doc comments explain each public method's inputs, result and errors.
Record decisions and trade-offs, such as why `ConflictPolicy` is a strategy.

parts.label: Visibility
parts.note: `+` public, `-` private, `#` protected. A JavaScript `#field` is private, so draw it with `-`.

parts.label: Name
parts.note: The method name, exactly as it appears in the code.

parts.label: Parameters
parts.note: Inputs the caller passes. Add types when they clarify the design.

parts.label: Return type
parts.note: What the method returns. Standard UML writes `: Booking`; Mermaid drops the colon.

code.title: Class diagram as text
code.caption: Mermaid class diagram source. Keeping the diagram as text lets it live in the repository and change with the code.

walk.text: A class box: one private field and two public methods.
`<<interface>>` marks `ConflictPolicy` as a contract, not a concrete class.
Plain arrows show that `BookingService` uses its collaborators.
`BookingService` notifies only the `BookingListener` interface; `NotificationService` and `AuditLogger` implement it, as built in c05-t06.
A dotted arrow with a hollow head means "implements".
A filled diamond is composition: rooms belong to one building.
Multiplicities say how many objects sit at each end of a link.

code.title: Doc comments on an interface
code.caption: JSDoc records the contract next to the code. Editors show it on hover.

walk.text: The class comment says what the interface decides, and tags it `@interface`.
Each parameter and the return value get one plain line.
The base method throws, so a missing override fails loudly.
The documented contract holds: back-to-back slots do not clash.

pitfalls: Do not draw every getter; show the members that explain the design.
Update diagrams when classes change, or readers will trust a wrong picture.
Do not use a composition diamond where objects outlive their owner.

options: A dotted line with a hollow triangle pointing to `ConflictPolicy`
No link, because interfaces are left off class diagrams
quiz.why: `StrictOverlapPolicy` implements the `ConflictPolicy` interface. UML draws realisation as a dotted line with a hollow triangle at the interface.

takeaway: Document the why, keep diagrams as text, and keep them current.
